sentences.text: The species name translates to 'one who walks on stilts,' a reference to the creature's exceptionally long and slender limbs.
This animal reached a total length of between 1.2 and 1.3 meters.
Its skull was lightly built, triangular in shape, and measured approximately 150 millimeters.
Measurements show the left forearm was longer than the upper arm, with lengths of 102 millimeters and 89 millimeters respectively.
The hindlimb featured a thigh bone measuring 144 millimeters and a shin bone measuring 130 millimeters.
One tooth in the lower jaw was so large it locked into a notch in the upper jaw.
Fossil evidence suggests a Dromicosuchus specimen was attacked by a larger rauisuchian predator before both animals died.
Scientists Hans-Dieter Sues and colleagues formally named this genus in the year 2003.
The stomach contents of the attacking predator included bones from an aetosaur, a cynodont, a dicynodont, and a possible temnospondyl.
Phylogenetic analysis places this sphenosuchian closest to Hesperosuchus and Kayentasuchus.
It belongs to the parent group known as Crocodylomorpha.
The animal is classified within the class Reptilia.
Remains were discovered in Upper Triassic rock formations within North Carolina, United States.
This reptile lived during the Carnian to Norian stages, approximately 237 to 205.7 million years ago.
